hint.text: Nonsensical means not having much meaning or making much sense.

atoms.text: Edward Lear was a famous British poet. He is known for writing funny, nonsensical limericks. Some people say that he is the creator of the limerick poem. He was born on the 12th of May 1812, near London, England. Before he was a poet, he enjoyed painting nature. Edward Lear began painting at 15 years old and liked to depict landscapes as well as animals. He also made drawings to go along with his poetry.

instruction.text: Decide if the following statements are true or false.

atoms.a: Edward Lear is famous for sad, emotional poems.

instruction.text: Match the parts of the sentences to complete them.

atoms.a: Edward Lear is famous for writing

example.a:
There was an old man in a tree,
Whose whiskers were lovely to see;
But the birds of the air,
Pluck'd them perfectly bare,
To make themselves nests on that tree.

trainers.instruction: Count the lines in the limerick.

atoms.b: A limerick is always <mat><gap>3 4 ++5</gap></mat> lines long.

instruction.text: Select the three longest lines of the limerick.

end.text: The first, second and fifth lines of a limerick are usually the longest, while the third and fourth lines are shorter.

instruction.text: Now, select all the lines that rhyme with the word free.

end.text: The first, second and fifth lines are not only the longest in a limerick, but they also rhyme with each other.

instruction.text: Select all the lines that rhyme with the word care.

end.text: The two shortest lines of a limerick also rhyme with each other.

instruction.text:
Most limericks start with “There is” or a similar phrase introducing a person or place in the first line.
Select all phrases that can be used to begin a limerick.
